title: The Best Classical Music For The Classroom
author: Michael Linsin
summary: In a lighter, personal post, Linsin shares his favorite classical music selections for the classroom, citing research-backed benefits like reduced stress and anxiety, improved memory, and enhanced concentration. He describes playing music as students enter and complete their first routine of the day to set tone and calm excitability, offering a list of specific pieces spanning the classical period and contemporary classical composers. He recommends downloading favorites to avoid ad interruptions and offers his preferred Pandora stations for readers who want a no-effort option, inviting readers to share their own favorite selections in the comments.
points: Cites research-backed benefits of classical music in class: reduced stress and anxiety, improved memory, increased productivity, and enhanced concentration.
Recommends playing music during entry and the first routine of the day to set tone and reduce excitability.
Provides a personal, curated list of both classical-period and contemporary classical pieces used in his own classroom.
Suggests downloading tracks rather than streaming to avoid ad interruptions during instructional time.
Offers specific Pandora station recommendations (Classical for Studying, Yo-Yo Ma, This Will Destroy You) for readers seeking a low-effort option.
quotes: reduce stress and anxiety. improve memory. increase productivity. enhance concentration. raise well-being. spark creativity.
I like to put the music on as students are entering the classroom and carrying out their first routine of the day.
It also has a strong calming effect and helps keep excitability at bay.
They’ve brought so much joy and peace to me and my students that I thought I’d share them with you—in no particular order.
I recommend downloading the pieces you like best from iTunes or Amazon so you’re not interrupted by annoying ads.
The research on classical music and stress is especially compelling, but I just like the way it makes me feel and how it gets me into a faster and deeper state of flow .
